summary: Postinstall and import-time dropper fetches and executes remote binary from obfuscated Cloudflare Workers hosts with DNS-TXT fallback
details: package.json declares a postinstall that runs setup.js. setup.js assembles dropper hostnames from arrays of string fragments joined at runtime (e.g. ["oob-wor","ker.cf","99-9b3.wor","kers",".dev"].join("")) to hide the destinations from static inspection, fetches a platform-specific opaque binary over HTTPS from anonymous Cloudflare Workers subdomains, and falls back to a DNS-TXT covert channel under *.dl.well1.site (querying c.<domain> for a chunk count, then iterating <i>.<domain> TXT records and base64-decoding the concatenation) when HTTP retrieval fails. The retrieved bytes are written to /var/tmp/.cache_<hex> on Unix or %TEMP%\dotnet_diag_<hex>.exe on Windows, chmodded 0755, and detached-executed via execFile. On Windows the script invokes powershell via execSync. index.js, declared as the package main, unconditionally require("./setup") inside a try/catch after exporting a trivial stub, so requiring or importing the package re-triggers the same download-and-execute chain even when installs are performed with --ignore-scripts. Cover-story naming (analytics_state, dotnet_diag) and DISABLE_TELEMETRY / DO_NOT_TRACK opt-out checks frame the drop as telemetry, but the destinations, fragment-splitting, DNS-TXT fallback, random staging paths, and detached execution of an unverified remote binary are inconsistent with legitimate telemetry.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
